svg.title: Support desk: how the pieces fit — SoftTrack web design mockup (#240)
svg.desc: The support desk epic as a map: how a request arrives, what a ticket for a customer carries, and how a ticket crosses from one team to another, with what stays out of scope, who reads what on a ticket, and the order the pieces land in.
svg.text: Support desk: how the pieces fit
· requests from outside, customers and response targets

g.text: three places, and what stays out
GETTING IN
How a request arrives, without anybody typing it in.
Email in
A message becomes a ticket; a reply becomes a comment.
A public request form
No account, and no place on the team.
ON THE TICKET
What a ticket for a customer carries.
Customers
Who a ticket is for. Mail and forms are matched by address.
Response targets
How long somebody has waited, in words.
Internal notes
Comments the customer never sees.
ACROSS TEAMS
From one team to another, without being on both.
Hand a ticket to a team
A request the other team accepts or declines.
Useful to every pair of teams, support or not. It comes first.
STILL OUT OF SCOPE
The line the roadmap drew, moved and not erased.

A configuration database, change and problem management, on-call rotas and paging, asset discovery, a service catalogue, approval workflows on requests, customer satisfaction surveys, and a workflow engine.
a ticket, from four places

svg.text: What an outside person can read is decided in the query and covered by a sweep test, the same as guests and finance.
A guest writes comments where #244 is on.

g.text: one first, then two chains

svg.text: before anybody outside reads a ticket
Off until a team turns it on: a team that does none of this sees none of it. Anything that accepts input from the internet is rate limited. This takes back a specific part of the
roadmap’s service-desk exclusion, and docs/roadmap.md changes with it. Each piece has its own mockup on its issue, #286 to #291.
